Quick technical summary (rough estimates):

Assumptions: target model = 13B-class open model (FP16 or 4-bit quant for cost), tokenization average: 1.2 chars/token approx.

1) Latency impact from context window
- For autoregressive decode, end-to-end latency = encode(input) + decode(output) + kv-cache ops per attention layer. Larger context windows increase memory and per-token attention compute roughly O(seq_length^2) for naive attention; with efficient attention kernels and caching, incremental decode cost mainly depends on output length, but first-token latency still requires key/value setup for the input (cost ~ O(input_len)).
- For 6k input + 1.5k output on a 13B model using optimized kernels and continuous batching, I estimate first-token latency in the 80-140ms range on an A100-class GPU with per-request isolated executor (no heavy colocation). p95 will depend on batching: aggressive batching increases p95; to hit p95 <= 300ms we need to keep batch sizes small for low-latency routes (max batch 4-8 depending on qps).

2) Streaming implications
- Streaming requires us to send tokens as they are decoded. That is favorable for UX but can slightly increase tail latency because we commit to lower decode batch sizes. Solution: hybrid routing — low-latency pool for interactive streaming (smaller batch sizes, dedicated instances) + high-throughput quantized pool for non-streaming batch jobs.

3) >8k tokens (long docs)
- For 8k-20k token inputs, recommend a chunk-and-retrieve approach: chunk docs and use an embedding/recall + rerank pipeline or use our long-context variant with specialized kernels and increased memory. Long-context serving increases per-request GPU memory and cost (can require larger instances or model sharding). For occasional long docs, an async batch pipeline is cost-effective.

4) Recommended config for FinCo (interactive):
- Model: 13B FP16 or 4-bit quant (vram permitting)
- Dedicated low-latency pool: 2-4 GPUs with small max batch (4) and autoscale headroom for bursts; p50 ~120ms realistic, p95 depends on concurrency but should be achievable <300ms with the above.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for multi-turns in the same session to reduce repeated encode cost.
- Streaming: enable on low-latency pool; for batch analytics route to dedicated high-throughput pool using model quantization and larger batches.

I'll prepare a quick slide with numbers for the Thursday readout. Attaching internal latency CSV with microbenchmarks.

— Dev
